papers.abstract_zh: 有效的 疫苗 沟通已成为全球卫生应急准备的一个决定性挑战,因为 疫苗 开发中的科学进步并未伴随着公众信任度的相应提升。最近 暴发(特别是埃博拉病毒、COVID-19 和 猴痘)的经验表明,当沟通不一致、错误信息激增以及公众对卫生机构的信心减弱时,仅靠 疫苗 的可用性不足以实现 疫苗 的高采用率。这篇叙述性评论批判性地综合了当前的证据,以检验公众信任的决定因素,评估现有 疫苗 传播策略的优势和局限性,并确定未来研究和政策的优先事项。该审查强调了有效 疫苗 沟通的五个相互关联的决定因素:机构透明度、基于证据的消息传递、值得信赖的社区伙伴关系、数字信息监控和持续的沟通适应。它还进一步确定了持续存在的挑战,包括反应性沟通方式、政治两极分化、获取可信信息的不平等以及人工智能驱动的错误信息日益增长的影响。目前的证据还受到横断面研究占主导地位、低收入和中等收入国家代表性不足以及对长期信任建设干预措施评估不足的限制。为了应对这些挑战,我们提出了自适应 疫苗 信任通信(AVTC)框架,该框架将 疫苗 通信概念化为一种连续的自适应过程,而不是单向的信息传输。通过整合机构透明度、基于证据的信息传递、值得信赖的社区伙伴关系、数字信息监测和持续反馈,该框架为加强公众信任、提高 疫苗 信心并加强对未来全球卫生紧急情况的准备提供了实用的路线图。

papers.title: Environmental surface and air contamination of MPXV in household and healthcare settings: a systematic review of detection and viability
papers.abstract: Mpox virus (MPXV) transmission primarily occurs through direct contact with infected skin lesions or body fluids. However, the 2022 and 2024 global outbreaks renewed concerns regarding the potential contribution of contaminated surfaces and air to transmission dynamics. This systematic review aimed to synthesize current evidence on environmental surface and air contamination of MPXV in household and healthcare settings. A systematic search of the literature was conducted to identify studies reporting environmental surface or air sampling for MPXV in clinical or household settings. Data were extracted on sampling methods, timing, detection metrics, and viral culture results. Surfaces were categorized into functional groups to allow cross-study comparison, and median Ct values were calculated when sample-level data were available. Healthcare worker (HCW) exposure and infection outcomes were also descriptively analysed. Twenty-three studies met the inclusion criteria. Across 391 direct patient-contact surfaces with analysable molecular data, 73.1% were PCR-positive for MPXV DNA. Among samples reporting Ct values, the median Ct was 32.2 (range: 16.1–39.0), while quantitative viral loads ranged from 0.301 to 5.38 log10 copies/cm2. Porous materials, particularly bedding and soft surfaces, demonstrated lower median Ct values compared to non-porous surfaces. Air sampling showed PCR positivity in over half of eligible samples, although viral loads were generally low. Viral culture was performed in a subset of studies, with viable virus recovered in a minority of samples, predominantly from surfaces with lower Ct values. Among 543 exposed healthcare workers, only 4 became infected without direct contact or sharps injury, despite documented environmental contamination in several settings. No additional HCW infections occurred during follow-up in most studies. Environmental contamination with MPXV DNA is frequently detectable in both household and healthcare settings. However, detection of viral DNA does not consistently correlate with viral viability, and confirmed occupational transmission among healthcare workers remains rare. Current evidence supports the predominance of direct contact transmission, while environmental contamination may represent a contextual amplification factor under specific conditions. Further studies incorporating standardized sampling methods and culture-based viability assessments are needed to better define the clinical relevance of environmental MPXV contamination.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on Monkeypox virus (MPXV) environmental contamination in household and healthcare settings. It finds frequent detection of MPXV DNA on surfaces (73.1% PCR-positive) and in air samples (over half PCR-positive), with porous materials showing higher contamination levels. However, viable virus recovery was rare and predominantly linked to lower Ct values, indicating limited correlation between DNA detection and infectivity. Despite environmental contamination, confirmed healthcare worker infections without direct contact were uncommon, suggesting direct contact remains the primary transmission route. Standardized sampling and viability assessments are needed to clarify the role of environmental contamination in transmission dynamics.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本系统综述检索了报告临床或家庭环境中 MPXV 环境表面或空气采样的研究,提取了有关采样方法、时间、检测指标和病毒培养结果的数据。23 项研究符合纳入标准,对 391 个表面和空气样本进行了基于分子和培养的分析。

papers.abstract_zh: 猴痘病毒 (MPXV) 传播 主要通过直接接触受感染的皮肤损伤或体液发生。然而,2022 年和 2024 年全球 暴发 再次引发了人们对受污染表面和空气对 传播 动态的潜在影响的担忧。本系统综述旨在综合有关家庭和医疗机构中 MPXV 环境表面和空气污染的最新证据。对文献进行了系统检索,以确定报告临床或家庭环境中 MPXV 环境表面或空气采样的研究。提取了有关采样方法、时间、检测指标和病毒培养结果的数据。将表面分类为功能组以进行交叉研究比较,并在样本水平数据可用时计算中位 Ct 值。还对医护人员 (HCW) 的暴露和感染结果进行了描述性分析。二十三项研究符合纳入标准。在具有可分析分子数据的 391 个直接与患者接触的表面中,73.1% 的 MPXV DNA PCR 呈阳性。在报告 Ct 值的样本中,中位 Ct 为 32.2(范围:16.1-39.0),而定量病毒载量范围为 0.301 至 5.38 log10 拷贝/cm2。与无孔表面相比,多孔材料,特别是床上用品和软表面,表现出较低的中位 Ct 值。尽管病毒载量普遍较低,但空气采样显示超过一半的合格样本呈 PCR 阳性。在一部分研究中进行了病毒培养,在少数样品中回收了活病毒,主要来自 Ct 值较低的表面。在 543 名暴露的医护人员中,只有 4 人在没有直接接触或锐器伤害的情况下被感染,尽管有记录显示在一些环境中存在环境污染。大多数研究在随访期间没有发生额外的医护人员感染。在家庭和医疗机构中,经常可以检测到 MPXV DNA 造成的环境污染。然而,病毒 DNA 的检测并不总是与病毒活力相关,并且在医护人员中确认的职业 传播 仍然很少。目前的证据支持直接接触 传播 的主导地位,而环境污染可能代表特定条件下的背景放大因素。需要进一步研究结合标准化采样方法和基于培养的活力评估,以更好地确定环境 MPXV 污染的临床相关性。

papers.title: A EVOLUÇÃO DOS EVENTOS PANDÊMICOS EM SAÚDE PÚBLICA: DESDE OS PRIMÓRDIOS DA HISTÓRIA ATÉ A ATUALIDADE
papers.abstract: A história da humanidade é marcada por eventos pandêmicos, epidêmicos e surtos que transcendem a crise sanitária, gerando também crises econômicas, políticas e sociais. Tais ocorrências são vistas como grandes desequilíbrios ecológicos, biológicos e sociais, cuja disseminação é potencializada pela mobilidade global de pessoas e bens. O objetivo deste artigo é analisar a progressão desses cenários globais que impactaram a Saúde Pública. A metodologia empregada foi uma revisão bibliográfica de natureza qualitativa, utilizando bases como a Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde e resultando na análise de 62 artigos científicos. Os resultados demonstram a evolução do conhecimento e das estratégias de enfrentamento ao longo do tempo. Na Antiguidade, prevaleciam as explicações religiosas e a queima de corpos, progredindo para a prática de quarentena na Idade Média e, com a ciência moderna, para o isolamento de agentes etiológicos e o uso de proteção individual. O estudo revisita cronologicamente eventos devastadores como a Peste de Atenas, a Peste Negra, Gripe Espanhola, HIV/AIDS, até as mais recentes pandemias de SARS, H1N1, Ebola, Covid-19 e Mpox. A pandemia de Covid-19 destacou a necessidade de se considerar esses eventos como fenômenos complexos, não-lineares e multipolares (clínica, econômica, social e política). Conclui-se que o enfrentamento requer aprendizado contínuo com a história e, no contexto brasileiro, o fortalecimento de um sistema de saúde público como o Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), valorizando a Atenção Primária em Saúde, o Programa Nacional de Imunização e a integração de ações de vigilância em saúde entre os entes federativos.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the historical evolution of pandemics and their multifaceted impacts on public health, economics, and society. It highlights the progression of responses from ancient religious explanations to modern strategies involving quarantine, isolation, and individual protection. The research emphasizes the complexity of pandemics, particularly in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, and underscores the importance of learning from history to strengthen public health systems, such as Brazil's SUS, and improve integrated health surveillance. The study is a qualitative literature review of 62 scientific articles, providing a broad overview of pandemic development without focusing on specific viral characteristics or detailed methodologies. While the findings offer insights into historical patterns and public health strategies, they do not provide target-specific evidence about the Mpox virus, which is a supplementary entity in this context.

What to know There are two types of the virus that causes monkeypox, clade I and clade II. Both types can be spread, treated, and prevented in the same ways. Each clade has two subclades (clade Ia and clade Ib; clade IIa and IIb). Recent outbreaks of monkeypox have spread initially through intimate or sexual contact. In some cases, monkeypox was then spread within households. There have been ongoing outbreaks of clade I monkeypox in Central and Eastern Africa since late 2023. Several Western European countries are reporting outbreaks that are likely related to the Central and Eastern African outbreaks but are affecting different people. Travel-associated clade I monkeypox cases have almost exclusively been attributed to subclade Ib; there have been no deaths associated with these cases and most people had relatively mild illness. The ongoing global outbreak of clade IIb monkeypox that began in 2022 has caused more than 100,000 cases in 122 total countries, including 115 countries where monkeypox was not previously reported. CDC has vaccination recommendations for people at risk in the United States or who are traveling to countries with clade I outbreaks or new clade II outbreaks. Current situation In the United States Clade I monkeypox The risk posed by the clade I monkeypox outbreak to most people within the United States remains low. Since November 2024, there have been more than 40 laboratory-confirmed cases of clade I monkeypox in the United States. Nearly all were diagnosed in people who: Had recently traveled from areas associated with the outbreak in Central and Eastern Africa; Had recently traveled from parts of Western Europe where newer outbreaks are being reported; OR Were linked to people who had traveled from these areas. We expect additional cases in Europe and the United States. Reminder Vaccination is an important tool in stopping the spread of monkeypox. If you have certain risk factors that make you eligible, you can help protect yourself from monkeypox by getting the 2-dose monkeypox vaccine. Monkeypox Vaccination Clade II monkeypox Clade II monkeypox is still circulating at low levels. Fall 2025 marked the highest monthly case counts since the peak of the outbreak in 2022. Clade I Monkeypox Outbreaks Cases of clade I monkeypox have been diagnosed worldwide. Clade II Monkeypox Outbreaks Clade II monkeypox is spreading in the United States and around the world. Across the globe Clade I monkeypox Outbreaks of clade I monkeypox in Central and Eastern Africa continue. Beginning in Fall 2025, several countries in Western Europe began reporting clade Ib monkeypox cases among individuals who had no documented history of international travel. These cases were likely related to male-to-male sexual contact. Other travel-associated cases of clade I monkeypox have been reported from other parts of Africa, as well as Asia, Europe, the Middle East, North America, South America, and Australia. Recent monkeypox outbreaks have low death rates During recent outbreaks, death rates ranged from than less than 0.5% (clade Ib) to about 3% (clade Ia). Clade II is the type that caused the ongoing global outbreak that began in 2022. Fewer than 0.1% of people infected with clade II die from the disease. Clade II monkeypox Several countries in West Africa have been experiencing an outbreak of clade II monkeypox since summer 2025. Travelers to Liberia and Ghana and should review the Travel Health Notice, which includes information about the monkeypox vaccine for eligible people. Global monkeypox case data For global case data for clade I and clade II monkeypox since January 1, 2024, see Global Mpox Trends. Confirmed cases include those that are laboratory confirmed as monkeypox virus and may include cases only confirmed as orthopoxvirus. These data are provided for situational awareness and are subject to change. What CDC is doing CDC raises awareness for U.S. healthcare providers, including the latest guidance for diagnosing monkeypox and clinical decision-making. CDC continues critical work to protect the United States from emerging and infectious diseases. CDC has collaborated closely with key partners in affected countries to help support efforts to stop monkeypox at the source. CDC works closely with U.S. state, tribal, local, and territorial public health departments to provide recommendations for clinical management, diagnosis, and prevention of domestic monkeypox cases. in the U.S. CDC continually increases capacity in communities across the United States for early detection of monkeypox through existing surveillance systems, including wastewater testing. CDC raises awareness for healthcare providers, including the latest guidance for diagnosing monkeypox and clinical decision-making. CDC collaborated with governmental and civil society partners in affected countries to collect and analyze case data, and to identify how monkeypox is spreading. CDC coordinated technical assistance in response to urgent in-country needs, including: increasing the number of monkeypox testing sites; improving specimen transport networks to quickly identify new cases; assisting with Ministry of Health-led vaccine implementation; strengthening emergency management systems; improving case surveillance; and training healthcare workers. CDC's staff throughout Africa provide critical, real-time information to inform U.S. preparedness efforts. In the United States CDC works closely with state, tribal, local, and territorial public health departments to provide recommendations for clinical management, diagnosis, and prevention of monkeypox cases in the U.S. CDC continually increases capacity in communities across the United States for early detection of monkeypox through existing surveillance systems, including wastewater testing. CDC raises awareness for healthcare providers, including the latest guidance for diagnosing monkeypox and clinical decision-making. CDC has information and recommendations for members of the public, including those traveling to Central or Eastern Africa: Travel Health Notice and Health Alert Network advisory. CDC continues to work with international partners to help reduce monkeypox transmission. analysis.time: Published 11 August 2026; event data cover 2022–2026 with ongoing outbreaks.
analysis.location_and_population: United States; Central and Eastern Africa; Western Europe; West Africa; global (122 countries).
analysis.event: CDC reports ongoing clade I and clade II mpox outbreaks with confirmed cases, travel-associated spread, and low death rates; guidance emphasizes vaccination and surveillance.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Clade IIb: >100,000 cases in 122 countries since 2022; <0.1% deaths. cases since Nov 2024; travel-linked; <0.5% (clade Ib) to ~3% (clade Ia) deaths. residents remains low.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: CDC provides vaccination recommendations, raises provider awareness, strengthens surveillance (including wastewater), and collaborates internationally to stop spread; data subject to change.

analysis.brief_en: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported on 11 August 2026 that mpox outbreaks caused by clade I and clade II viruses continue to circulate globally. The clade IIb outbreak that began in 2022 has exceeded 100,000 cases across 122 countries, with fewer than 0.1% of patients dying. In the United States, more than 40 laboratory-confirmed clade I cases have been detected since November 2024, nearly all linked to travel from Central/Eastern Africa or Western Europe or to contacts of travelers; no deaths have been reported among these cases. What to know There have been outbreaks of clade I monkeypox in Central and Eastern Africa since late 2023. Since January 2024, more than 55,000 confirmed cases of clade I monkeypox have been reported globally, including more than 150 deaths. Newer outbreaks in several Western European countries are likely related to this ongoing outbreak. Transmission dynamics are changing. Only a small proportion of exported clade I monkeypox cases worldwide this year have originated in Central or Eastern African countries. Recent travel-associated clade I monkeypox cases have almost exclusively been attributed to subclade Ib; there have been no deaths associated with these cases and available data have detailed relatively mild disease courses. Outbreak overview In the United States The risk posed by the clade I monkeypox outbreak to most people within the United States remains low. The risk to men who have sex with men is low to moderate. Clade I cases in the United States have increased in frequency since March 2026. As of July 2026, there have been more than 40 clade I monkeypox cases reported in the United States. Nearly all U.S. cases were diagnosed in people who: Had recently traveled to areas associated with the outbreak in Central and Eastern Africa; Had recently traveled to parts of Western Europe where newer outbreaks are being reported; OR Were linked to people who had traveled from these areas. CDC expects additional cases in Europe and the United States. Preventing Monkeypox While Traveling Learn where monkeypox is spreading and how to lower your risk of getting it during travel. In Central and Eastern Africa Clade Ia monkeypox outbreaks began impacting western areas of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in 2024. Available data indicate that clade Ia monkeypox has spread through sexual contact, regular household contact, and encounters with infected dead or live wild animals. Clade Ib monkeypox cases initially impacted eastern areas of DRC in late 2023. This subclade has driven much of the spread throughout Central and Eastern Africa and most travel-associated cases to other parts of the world. Available data indicate that these cases at first spread through heterosexual intimate or sexual contact between adults, then spread likely occurred within households, including to children. The disease spread in 2024 and 2025 to neighboring countries of DRC, only some of which are endemic for the virus that causes monkeypox, and sustained local spread occurred. As of April 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo is still the country with the majority of clade Ib cases. Outside Central and Eastern Africa Several countries in other parts of Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, and South America, as well as Australia, have confirmed clade I monkeypox cases mostly in travelers who'd recently been in areas with clade I outbreaks. To date, there have been more than 300 clade Ib cases in high-income countries, and no deaths have been reported. Beginning in Fall 2025, several countries in Western Europe began reporting clade Ib monkeypox cases among individuals who had no documented history of international travel. These cases were likely related to intimate or sexual exposure among men who have sex with men. We expect additional cases in Europe and the United States. For data since January 1, 2024, see 2022-24 Monkeypox (Monkeypox) Outbreak: Global Trends (shinyapps.io). Confirmed cases include those that are laboratory confirmed as monkeypox virus and may include cases only confirmed as orthopoxvirus. These data are provided for situational awareness and are subject to change. Clade I monkeypox and children Early in the Central and Eastern African outbreak, a high proportion of suspected cases in some areas were reported in children younger than 15 years of age. Historically, cases of monkeypox in children where monkeypox occurs regularly often happen after contact with wild animals that carry the disease. People then can spread the disease to close contacts, including in their households. The number of children with suspected monkeypox in this outbreak is probably due to spread within and between close households, the large number of younger people in affected countries, misdiagnosis of other diseases (such as measles), poor sanitary conditions, limited access to health services, and a high level of food insecurity and malnutrition. Based on what we know today, we don't expect to see the same sort of pattern in the United States for several reasons, including smaller household sizes, access to cleaning and disinfecting products, and improved access to medical care, equipment, and information about preventing spread while caring for patients. Notably, there are no consistent reports of schools as drivers of monkeypox transmission during any recent outbreaks. If cases of clade I monkeypox do happen in children the United States, CDC has clinical and public health guidance for reporting, testing, and effective case management. What CDC is doing CDC has been supporting DRC monkeypox research and response for more than 20 years. CDC and other U.S. government agencies have continued working in-country with partners in affected areas on disease surveillance, building local laboratory capacity, strengthening public health and laboratory workforce capacity, case investigation, case management, infection prevention and control, border health, and risk communication and community engagement. CDC staff brought laboratory supplies and trained local staff on laboratory equipment Resources Monkeypox in the United States and Around the World: Current Situation There are outbreaks of clade I and clade II monkeypox around the world. analysis.summary_en: The CDC reports ongoing outbreaks of clade I monkeypox in Central and Eastern Africa since late 2023, with global confirmed cases exceeding 55,000 since January 2024, including over 150 deaths. Newer outbreaks have emerged in Western European countries and the United States, with more than 40 cases reported in the U.S. as of July 2026. Transmission occurs through sexual contact, household interactions, and animal exposure. The risk to most people in the U.S. is low, though it is moderate for men who have sex with men. Clade Ib has been the dominant subclade driving spread, with no deaths reported in high-income countries. The CDC is actively monitoring and responding to these outbreaks, providing guidance for case management and prevention. The data are subject to change and are intended for situational awareness.

news.content: Mpox hospitalisations highlight disparities as case patterns shift in Europe Friday, 14 August 2026 By The Brussels Times Newsroom Credit: Unsplash Mpox cases in the EU/EEA held broadly steady in July, with 153 infections linked to clade I of the virus reported by 12 countries. This is according to new surveillance figures show from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) released on Friday. Portugal reported the largest number of clade I cases in July, with 68, while France recorded the most clade II cases, with seven. Overall clade I case numbers changed little month to month, with 159 cases reported in June and 162 in May. Clade II infections continued to fall, with 12 cases reported in July compared with 28 in June and 38 in May. Across the past 12 months (August 2025 to July 2026), EU/EEA countries reported 1,083 clade I cases and 888 clade II cases, with 20 countries reporting clade I and 19 reporting clade II. Most cases with complete information were reported among men who have sex with men — 89% of clade I cases and 91% of clade II cases. Hospitalisations and deaths Hospital admission was reported for 12% of clade I cases with complete information and 8% of clade II cases with complete information, the ECDC said. Two deaths were reported among people infected with clade II in the past 12 months, while no deaths were reported among people infected with clade I. Among cases with known vaccination status, 22% of clade I cases and 20% of clade II cases had received two vaccine doses. The ECDC said the number of clade I cases “remains relatively stable” in the EU/EEA, while clade II cases “continue to decline”. Short-term trend analysis is limited because clade information is missing for a substantial share of reported cases and some case details may be updated later, the agency added. analysis.brief_en: European mpox surveillance data released on 14 August 2026 show clade I cases holding steady while clade II infections continue to fall across the EU/EEA. Over the past year, 1,083 clade I and 888 clade II cases were reported, with 89–91% occurring among men who have sex with men. Hospitalisation rates reached 12% for clade I and 8% for clade II, and two clade II deaths were recorded, while no clade I fatalities were reported. Vaccination coverage with two doses stood at 22% for clade I and 20% for clade II cases. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control cautioned that trend analysis is constrained by incomplete clade typing and potential data revisions.

news.content_title: NYC reports rise in Mpox Clade I cases among travelers returning from overseas
news.content: Matthew Euzarraga Updated Sat, August 15, 2026 at 12:19 AM UTC 0 Editor's note: The video above aired in a previous newscast. NEW YORK (PIX11) – New York City is seeing an uptick in cases of an infectious disease that causes a painful rash, known as mpox clade I, especially among those returning from overseas travel in Europe, according to the NYC Department of Mental Hygiene. “We have seen recent cases of clade I mpox among people returning from travel to Europe,” read a social post from the agency posted on Friday afternoon. “If you're traveling to Europe and may be sexually active with new partners while there, make sure to get both doses of the JYNNEOS mpox vaccine before you go.” Discover more local reporting on our homepage The first known case of mpox clade I in the city was reported in March. An individual who tested positive for the virus had traveled internationally, according to NYC health officials. Within the last month, 14 cases of Mpox have been reported in the city, according to data What is Mpox? Formerly known as monkeypox, mpox is a viral illness caused by the monkeypox virus. Common symptoms of mpox are a skin rash or lesions, which can last two to four weeks. Fever, headache, muscle aches, back pain, low energy, and swollen lymph nodes are also common, according to the World Health Organization . Mpox spreads from person to person through close contact with someone who has mpox, including household members. Close contact includes skin-to-skin, kissing, and sexual contact, according to the WHO. Though anyone can test positive for mpox, globally the disease has affected primarily gay, bisexual, and men who have sex with men, according to the World Health Organization . Mpox Vaccination The NYC Health Department recommends completing the two-dose JYNNEOS series . If you’ve already received the first dose, it is never too late to get the second, health officials noted. If you have already been vaccinated, there is no recommendation to receive a booster, according to current health guidance. If you have already tested positive for mpox, you should already be immune, according to health officials. For more information on mpox, click here. WHO's top monkeypox expert Dr. Rosamund Lewis said she doesn’t expect the hundreds of cases reported to date to turn into another pandemic, but acknowledged there are still many unknowns about the disease, including how exactly it’s spreading and whether the suspension of mass smallpox immunization decades ago may somehow be speeding its transmission. (Cynthia S. Goldsmith, Russell Regner/CDC via AP, File) By: Justin Boggs Posted 2:24 PM, Jun 14, 2022 and last updated 2:51 PM, Jun 14, 2022 Despite recent cases of monkeypox throughout the globe, the World Health Organization said Tuesday it is recommending against mass vaccinations for the disease "at this time." The guidance comes as the WHO debates using smallpox vaccines as a way to prevent the spread of monkeypox. "While smallpox vaccines are expected to provide some protection against monkeypox, there is limited clinical data, and limited supply," said Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, director-general of the WHO. 1/1 Skip Ad Continue watchingafter the adVisit Advertiser websiteGO TO PAGE Instead, the WHO is recommending targeted vaccinations for those at high risk of contracting the virus and those who have been exposed to it. In guidance issued Tuesday by the WHO, the organization is recommending those who are exposed to the virus should get vaccinated within four days of first exposure to prevent onset of the disease. The WHO recommends vaccines for health workers at risk, laboratory personnel working with orthopoxviruses, clinical laboratory staff performing diagnostic testing for monkeypox and others who may be at risk as per national policy. "Any decision about whether to use vaccines should be made jointly by individuals who may be at risk and their health care provider, based on an assessment of risks and benefits, on a case-by-case basis,” said Tedros. Tedros said there have been 1,600 cases of monkeypox reported worldwide. The virus has been detected in more than three dozen countries, including 32 that are newly affected. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said the risk of monkeypox to the public is low but you should avoid contact with others if you develop an unexplained skin rash. Typical symptoms of monkeypox include a rash, fever, malaise, headache and muscle aches. analysis.brief_en: The World Health Organization advised on 14 June 2022 against mass mpox vaccinations, instead endorsing targeted post-exposure immunization within four days for people at high risk or with known exposure. WHO’s director-general and top monkeypox expert emphasized limited vaccine supply and clinical evidence, and recommended case-by-case risk-benefit discussions between patients and clinicians. As of the guidance, 1,600 mpox cases had been reported across more than three dozen countries, with the U.S. CDC assessing the public risk as low. Typical symptoms include rash, fever, malaise, headache, and muscle aches. WHO also highlighted ongoing uncertainty about transmission routes and the possible role of waning smallpox immunity.

news.content_title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
news.content: Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak. The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk. Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox , with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far. Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023. High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk. “Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development . “However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can. “This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal. Mpox vaccines can be difficult to procure in countries like Madagascar, which is the world’s fifth-poorest country. - Simon Townsley The WHO has previously endorsed fractional dosing, where vials of vaccine are divided into smaller parts, during health emergencies. The approach – which was used in the UK during Covid – is generally considered a safe and effective way of protecting populations when vaccine supplies are limited. The method was authorised during yellow fever outbreaks in Angola and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and was also used for mpox vaccines in the US and UK in the summer of 2022, during an outbreak involving a different strain of the virus that primarily affected gay and bisexual men. Several clinical trials have found that, when administered correctly, fractional doses of mpox vaccine can provide protection comparable to full doses. But the approach also carries associated risks. One concern is the need for thousands of extra needles and syringes, increasing the risk of accidental needle re-use and the transmission of blood-borne infections such as HIV. “Madagascar has had to acquire many more needles and syringes because normally one dose is attached to one vaccine,” said Dr Bansal. Fractional doses of a standard vaccine must be administered intradermally – into the top layer of the skin – rather than into the muscle. The skin contains specialised immune cells that can trigger a strong immune response, allowing smaller quantities of vaccine to be used. But intradermal injections are considerably more difficult to administer than injections into the muscle. They require skilled vaccinators to ensure the vaccine is delivered at the correct depth. They are also more likely to cause local reactions, including swelling and itching, and can sometimes leave a distinctive raised “wheel” on the skin – similar to the scars left by the BCG vaccine for tuberculosis which many people received as children before the disease was eradicated in the UK in 1980. Public health officials within Madagascar remain hopeful that they will receive additional vaccine supplies in the coming months, helping to curb an epidemic that has overwhelmed local hospitals and clinics over the past four months. But mpox vaccines are expensive, costing between $50 and $140 per dose, and can be difficult to procure in low-income countries such as Madagascar, which is the world’s fifth-poorest country. The 60,000 doses delivered to the island so far have been funded largely by Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, and the WHO. Both organisations have faced significant funding shortfalls over the past year as governments, including those of the UK and US, have reduced their spending on global health. Mpox typically causes flu-like symptoms and a painful rash of swollen lesions that can spread across the entire body. For people living with HIV, the virus is particularly dangerous and can lead to severe complications, including brain inflammation, severe bacterial infections of lesions and, in rare cases, can result in death. It spreads mostly through very close physical contact, including sexual contact and through sharing towels and bed sheets. In poor countries, where people often live in closer quarters and have less access to simple infection control measures like soap and clean water, outbreaks can be particularly difficult to control. High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. File photo Rare viral infection that can spread from person to person, caused by monkeypox virus, also reported in Australia, Canada, US At least eight countries in the World Health Organization European Region have reported cases of monkeypox in recent days, while Australia, Canada, and the US have also reported similar cases, the WHO said Friday. The European countries that in recent days reported monkeypox – a rare viral infection that can be spread from person to person and is caused by the monkeypox virus – are Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, and the UK. "These recent cases are atypical for several reasons," said Hans Kluge, WHO regional director for Europe. "In this instance, all but one of the recent cases have no relevant travel history to areas where monkeypox is endemic, in West Africa or Central Africa," he said. Kluge also said that most of the initial cases found were detected through sexual health services and are among men who had sex with men. "Because of the geographically dispersed nature of the cases across Europe and beyond, the transmission may have been ongoing for some time," he said. Kluge said WHO is working with concerned countries to investigate cases further, determine the likely source of infection, how the virus is spreading, and limit further transmission. "We are also providing guidance and support on surveillance, testing, infection prevention and control, clinical management, risk communication, and community engagement, as well as facilitating information sharing across countries and health networks," said Kluge. He said most of the cases currently under investigation in Europe are mild. - Self-limiting illness Monkeypox is usually a self-limiting illness, and most of those infected will recover within a few weeks without treatment. "However, the disease can be more severe, especially in young children, pregnant women, and immunocompromised individuals," said the WHO regional chief. According to Kluge, people with suspected monkeypox should be investigated and isolated on the first appearance of symptoms. "Monkeypox does not normally spread easily between humans, and requires close contact, with the virus entering the body through broken skin, the respiratory tract, eyes, nose and mouth, and via bodily fluids," he said. It can spread through close physical contact, including sexual contact, with someone who has monkeypox. "As we enter the summer season in the European Region, with mass gatherings, festivals, and parties, I am concerned that transmission could accelerate, as the cases currently being detected are among those engaging in sexual activity, and the symptoms are unfamiliar to many," said Kluge. Show results from: Clear search input Search for result Max Clear search input Search for result Article Mpox Awareness Helps a Monze Mother Protect Her Children How Mpox awareness is helping families recognise symptoms early, seek care promptly and protect their children and communities Tikulirekuti Banda UNICEF Zambia/2026/Mwenya 14 August 2026 MONZE, Southern Province, Zambia, August 2026 --- In Kazombo community, Monze District, Caren Mutinta, a mother of two, says she had never heard about Mpox until community-based volunteers (CBVs) visited her household. The visit was part of an integrated risk communication, community engagement and community-based surveillance intervention supported by UNICEF, with funding from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (US CDC), to strengthen Mpox preparedness and early detection in Southern Province. Implemented between April and June 2026, the intervention covered Monze, Kazungula, Livingstone and Chikankata districts. “Before the community people came to sensitize us, we hadn’t known about Mpox,” Caren recalls. “After sensitization, we came to know what Mpox looks like.” During the household visit, the volunteers noticed rashes on her two children. Because they had been trained to identify signs and symptoms that could resemble Mpox, they advised her to take the children to the clinic immediately. When these people came to sensitize us on Mpox, they found my children with symptoms that looked like Mpox, Caren further says. I was told to take my children to the clinic. Then I took them the same day. At Chisekese Rural Health Centre, health workers assessed the children and confirmed that the condition was not Mpox. The children were treated for rashes and given medicine. “They were treated and given medicine,” Caren says. “From that time, there has been no other problem; they are okay.” UNICEF Zambia/2026/Mwenya Caren Mutinta and her family during an interview with UNICEF staff Tikulirekuti Banda. For Chinyama Miriam Buku, Facility In-Charge at Chisekese Rural Health Centre, this example shows how community sensitization strengthened early detection and timely care-seeking. “Through the programme, we were able to identify suspected cases early and support timely referral and treatment,” she says. “We were able to do this because of the programme.” UNICEF Zambia/2026/Mwenya Chinyama Mirriam Buku, Health Facility In Charge, Chisekese rural health centre, Monze. She adds that CBVs played a critical role in reaching households directly with lifesaving information. In the Chisekese catchment area, the programme reached approximately 1,588 households and 8,587 people, while also sensitizing truck drivers and engaging headmen, pregnant women, and mothers of children under five. “The programme was a success,” Buku says. “Our community is now able to identify the signs and symptoms of Mpox, and we are confident they will report to the facility if they suspect anything related to Mpox.” The CBVs played a critical role in taking lifesaving Mpox information directly to households and strengthening community-based surveillance. Through the training, CBVs were equipped to identify possible signs and symptoms of Mpox and explain how it spreads and can be prevented and encourage families to seek care early when they notice symptoms of concern. For Cletus Mukonka, one of the trained CBVs, the training gave volunteers the confidence to move from house to house and engage communities with clear and accurate information. We were trained in Mpox by UNICEF, and after being trained, we were deployed in the community to start sensitization on Mpox: the signs and symptoms, how it spreads, and how we can prevent it. UNICEF Zambia/2026/Mwenya Cletus Mukonka and Judith Biemba, Community based volunteers conducting door to door sensitizations in Kazombo village Monze. For Sebastian Siyamwenga, village headman of Kazombo, engaging local leaders early helped strengthen community acceptance of the Mpox sensitization activities. UNICEF Zambia/2026/Mwenya Sebastian Siyamwenga, village headman of Kazombo village in Monze. We thank the health facility for engaging us in this programme to sensitize the community on the signs and symptoms of Mpox. We are very happy that they engaged us early enough in this programme. At provincial level, the intervention also demonstrated the value of community-based surveillance, timely risk communication, and collaboration between health workers, CBVs, community leaders, and partners. “Between April and June, Southern Province captured 19 suspected cases of Mpox, and all these cases were referred to health facilities. Although surveillance was heightened, none of the 19 cases met the case definition of Mpox,” Dr. Calistus Kayunga, Provincial Health Director, Southern Province said. As final remarks, the Provincial Health Director said the intervention showed the value of strong partnerships in bringing lifesaving information and services closer to communities. UNICEF Zambia/2026/Mwenya Tikulirekuti Banda-UNICEF, with Dr. Calistus Kayunga, Provincial Health Director, Southern Province. “The reach and impact of this project cannot be overemphasized. It made a huge difference within a short period by reaching our people and showing what can be achieved when we work together with partners. Through strong collaboration, we can design and implement interventions that positively impact the communities we serve,” Dr. Calistus Kayunga said. For Caren Mutinta, the impact was immediate and personal: she received information, acted quickly, and her children were treated on time. Her experience shows how integrated door-to-door sensitizations can move communities from limited awareness to early action, protecting families while strengthening disease surveillance at community level. Show results from: Clear search input Search for result Max Clear search input Search for result Article Reaching People on the Move with Mpox Information That Protects Through tailored risk communication, communities on the move are gaining the knowledge they need to prevent mpox and seek care when symptoms arise Tikulirekuti Banda UNICEF Zambia/2026/Mwenya 14 August 2026 MONZE District, Zambia, August 2026 --- Across Southern Province, long-distance truck drivers move goods between Zambia and neighbouring countries including South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, Zimbabwe and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). As they travel long distances and interact with different people along transport routes, they can face increased exposure to public health risks. Thus, drivers need clear and practical information on public health risks including diseases like Mpox. They require information on how to protect themselves from and prevent themselves from catching diseases and on recognizing symptoms early and seeking care in time. UNICEF, with support from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, partnered with the Ministry of Health through the Southern Provincial Health Office to implement integrated Mpox activities between April and June 2026. The activities focused on communities along the international trucking route from Southern Africa towards the mining towns in the Copperbelt and Northwestern Zambia. The response package included risk communication, community engagement, community-based surveillance, and hygiene promotion and infection prevention and control in Chikankata, Monze, Livingstone and Kazungula, districts that sit along an international trucking route from Southern Africa. Chikankata district lies on the trucking route and hosts the Zambia Revenue Authority’s truckers’ dry port, these factors made it one of the obvious support site. UNICEF Zambia/2026/Mwenya Dr. Kanunga Kazhila, Acting District Health Director, Chikankata District Health Office. We conducted this programme as Chikankata district. We are a transit district with a transit population whose composition is full of traders and people who are both from within the country and out of the country. The programme was beneficial in that every community was sensitised about the importance of looking out for the signs and symptoms of Mpox. For drivers such as Joseph Muzikiti, the sensitization offered information that could be used immediately and passed on to others. Joseph, who has driven through South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Zambia and the DRC for nine years, said the knowledge was useful because drivers spend much of their time moving across borders. “I have learnt a lot about Mpox,” Joseph said. “You know, us truck drivers, we travel a lot, and we are at risk of too much Mpox. The knowledge that I have about Mpox now, I can even teach the other drivers about it.” UNICEF Zambia/2026/Mwenya Long-distance truck driver Joseph Muzikiti poses in front of his truck in Monze. The message also helped drivers move from general awareness to practical prevention. White Paiva first heard about Mpox while travelling in the DRC, where he understood it mainly as a contagious disease. UNICEF Zambia/2026/Mwenya White Paiva, truck driver speaking with the community-based volunteers from his truck in Southern Province. I first heard about Mpox in Congo DRC and knew it was contagious. But I did not know that simple hygiene and prevention practices could reduce the risk of infection. Now I know that, as truck drivers, we need to recognize symptoms early, avoid close contact with suspected cases, maintain hygiene and seek care quickly if we suspect illness. For Lovely Mukupa, who has worked as a truck driver for 19 years, the session filled an important information gap. “This is the best programme because you are educating us on how not to contract the disease and how it can be treated,” Lovely said. “It is the first time someone is educating us on Mpox.” Her experience reflects the value of bringing trusted health information directly to drivers who may not always be reached through routine communication channels. UNICEF Zambia/2026/Mwenya White Paiva, truck driver with Community Based Volunteers from Nansenga health facility, Chikankanta district Together, these voices show why Mpox risk communication is critical for mobile populations. For truck drivers, long journeys, cross-border movement, and regular interaction with different people can increase exposure to communicable disease risks. By prioritizing drivers with clear information on symptoms, prevention, hygiene and when to seek care, UNICEF and partners helped ensure that lifesaving messages travel with the people who keep goods moving across the region. news.content_title: 广州八院唐小平、于海生团队关于猴痘病毒的最新研究
news.content: 顶部 首页 首页 晴 / 21° 隐私 广州八院唐小平、于海生团队关于猴痘病毒的最新研究 病毒学界 近日,广州医科大学附属市八医院唐小平教授、于海生教授团队联合山西农业大学动物医学学院庞全海团队,在《BMC Microbiology》发表题为“Pathogenic Signatures and Therapeutic Evaluation of Emergent MPXV Clade Ib in Low-Susceptibility and Immunocompromised Mouse Models” 研究论文。 该研究围绕新发的猴痘病毒Clade Ib,建立了覆盖不同遗传背景和免疫状态的小鼠感染模型(C57BL/6小鼠、 BALB/c小鼠、Stat1基因敲除小鼠和AGB6小鼠),系统比较了不同小鼠对猴痘病毒的易感性、宿主免疫转录特征以及Clade Ib与Clade IIb的致病差异,并进一步评价了抗病毒药物特考玮瑞的抗病毒效果,为猴痘病毒Clade Ib的致病机制研究和抗病毒干预评价提供了可重复、易操作的实验平台。 (新发Clade Ib带来新的公共卫生挑战) 展开剩余 85 % 四种小鼠呈现不同感染结局 研究团队采用鼻猴痘病毒主要分为Clade I和Clade II,其中又可进一步划分为Ia、Ib、IIa和IIb等亚分支。 2022年全球猴痘疫情主要是Clade IIb,而2023年在刚果出现了Clade Ib,随后持续传播并扩散至非洲以外地区。与Clade IIb相比,Clade Ib被认为与更严重的临床结局和持续的人际传播有关,对儿童、孕妇及免疫功能低下人群构成更大威胁。 然而,传统非人灵长类动物模型成本高、实验周期长,CAST/EiJ等易感小鼠又存在繁殖困难、供应受限等问题。因此,建立来源稳定、操作方便且能够反映不同疾病严重程度的小鼠模型,特别是建立评价疫苗小鼠模型,是开展猴痘病毒研究的迫切需求。 内接种方式,以相同剂量的MPXV Clade Ib感染四种不同遗传背景的小鼠(C57BL/6小鼠、 BALB/c小鼠、Stat1基因敲除小鼠和AGB6小鼠),结果显示,四种小鼠感染后均出现不同程度的体重下降,但疾病结局存在明显差异。 其中,STAT1缺失小鼠表现出最高易感性,在感染后第8天前后达到100%死亡;AGB6小鼠死亡率约为40%。相比之下,C57BL/6和BALB/c小鼠虽然出现一过性体重下降,但均能够存活并逐渐恢复,表现为自限性感染。 病毒学和病理学检测进一步发现,病毒能够在小鼠鼻甲和肺组织中有效复制。肺组织中的病毒抗原主要分布于支气管上皮及其周围炎症细胞,STAT1缺失小鼠的病毒抗原信号和肺部损伤最为明显。这些结果提示,宿主干扰素信号通路是限制Clade Ib复制和疾病进展的重要防线。 (Stat1敲除小鼠、AGB6 小鼠与野生型小鼠对猴痘病毒 Ib 分支的易感性差异) 不同遗传背景决定不同免疫响应节奏 为了进一步解析宿主免疫反应,研究团队对感染后不同时间点的C57BL/6和BALB/c小鼠脾脏进行了转录组测序。 结果显示,C57BL/6小鼠能够较早启动强烈的抗病毒反应。感染后第3天,便可检测到大量差异表达基因,Oas1a、Rtp1和Ligp1等抗病毒相关基因明显上调;感染后第5天,差异表达基因数量达到峰值。相比之下,BALB/c小鼠的转录反应出现得更晚,整体幅度也相对较弱。 值得注意的是,尽管两种小鼠均激活了干扰素和炎症相关通路,但其适应性免疫相关基因却出现不同程度下调。 C57BL/6小鼠主要表现为淋巴细胞分化和功能相关通路受抑,而BALB/c小鼠则更多表现为MHC抗原加工与呈递通路下调。 进入恢复期后,C57BL/6小鼠逐渐启动细胞增殖、细胞外基质重塑和组织修复相关程序;BALB/c小鼠则在较晚阶段出现免疫球蛋白介导的免疫反应。 这说明,Clade Ib感染不仅能诱导强烈的先天免疫和炎症反应,还可能伴随适应性免疫相关程序的暂时抑制,而这种免疫失衡具有明显的宿主遗传背景差异。 (C57BL/6与Balb/c小鼠感染猴痘病毒Ib分支后脾脏转录组的时间动态变化) Clade Ib表现出更快的感染进程 研究团队进一步在易感的Stat1缺失小鼠中,以相同感染剂量和相同实验条件比较了Clade Ib与Clade IIb的毒力。 结果显示,与Clade IIb相比,Clade Ib感染后小鼠体重下降出现得更早,疾病进展更快,肺组织病毒载量更高,病毒抗原分布也更加广泛。 转录组分析发现,Clade Ib感染伴随更明显的组织损伤和炎症相关表达特征,包括Mmp8和S100a3等基因上调。同时,干扰素应答、抗原加工与呈递等免疫相关通路呈现更广泛的下调。 不过,在所检测时间点的肺组织病理评分并未出现显著差异。综上所述,现有结果支持Clade Ib在该模型中具有更快的感染动力学和更强的复制能力。 (Stat1 基因敲除小鼠中猴痘病毒Ib 分支与 IIb 分支的致病性比较) 特考玮瑞显著抑制病毒复制 为了验证这些小鼠模型是否可用于抗病毒药物评价,研究团队选择正痘病毒抑制剂特考玮瑞进行体内实验。 在C57BL/6、AGB6和Stat1缺失小鼠中,特考玮瑞均能够减轻感染后的体重下降,并明显降低肺组织中的病毒载量和病毒抗原水平。 组织病理学结果也显示,药物处理后小鼠肺组织结构保存更完整,炎症、坏死及其他感染相关损伤得到改善。 转录组结果表明,特考玮瑞治疗还可减弱病毒感染引起的大规模转录重塑,使宿主转录状态向创伤修复和恢复相关程序转变。 需要注意的是,本研究中的特考玮瑞在感染当天即开始给药,属于非常早期的干预模式。 (验证AGB6、Stat1缺失以及C57BL/6 小鼠作为猴痘病毒 Ib 分支药物评价模型的适用性) 研究意义 本研究建立了野生型、干扰素受体缺失和STAT1缺失小鼠Clade Ib感染的模型体系。 不同模型可满足不同研究需求: 野生型小鼠适合用于研究非致死性病毒复制、宿主免疫反应,以及药物和疫苗评价; AGB6小鼠可用于研究中度至重度感染; Stat1缺失小鼠则能够形成快速进展的致死性疾病,适合开展致病性和抗病毒药物的初步体内评价。 研究还从转录组层面揭示了Clade Ib感染过程中“先天免疫和炎症激活-适应性免疫相关程序下调-组织修复启动”的动态变化,为理解宿主遗传背景、干扰素信号和疾病严重程度之间的关系提供了实验数据。 作者信息 广州医科大学附属市八医院与山西农业大学联合培养博士生韩红宇、硕士生王肖玮为该论文共同第一作者,广州医科大学附属市八医院唐小平教授、于海生教授和山西农业大学庞全海教授为本文的共同通讯作者。 于海生教授,广州医科大学附属市八医院PI,传染病研究所副所长(主持工作),生物安全三级实验室副主任。长期从事新突发病毒的感染与免疫相关研究,致力于树突状细胞在病毒感染中作用、中和抗体研发以及研究高致病性病毒的致病机理。以第一作者或通讯作者在Molecular Therapy(2026)、National Science Review(2025)、Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy(2023)、Nature Communications(2023)、JCI Insight(2020)等杂志发表 SCI 文章50余篇。主持或参与国家传染病重大专项、省自然科学基金、科技攻关专项等项目。 Free web novels for online reading. 评论 全部 还没有人评论过,快来抢首评 抢首评 推荐阅读 news.content_original: 顶部 首页 首页 晴 / 21° 隐私 广州八院唐小平、于海生团队关于猴痘病毒的最新研究 病毒学界 近日,广州医科大学附属市八医院唐小平教授、于海生教授团队联合山西农业大学动物医学学院庞全海团队,在《BMC Microbiology》发表题为“Pathogenic Signatures and Therapeutic Evaluation of Emergent MPXV Clade Ib in Low-Susceptibility and Immunocompromised Mouse Models” 研究论文。 该研究围绕新发的猴痘病毒Clade Ib,建立了覆盖不同遗传背景和免疫状态的小鼠感染模型(C57BL/6小鼠、 BALB/c小鼠、Stat1基因敲除小鼠和AGB6小鼠),系统比较了不同小鼠对猴痘病毒的易感性、宿主免疫转录特征以及Clade Ib与Clade IIb的致病差异,并进一步评价了抗病毒药物特考玮瑞的抗病毒效果,为猴痘病毒Clade Ib的致病机制研究和抗病毒干预评价提供了可重复、易操作的实验平台。 (新发Clade Ib带来新的公共卫生挑战) 展开剩余 85 % 四种小鼠呈现不同感染结局 研究团队采用鼻猴痘病毒主要分为Clade I和Clade II,其中又可进一步划分为Ia、Ib、IIa和IIb等亚分支。 2022年全球猴痘疫情主要是Clade IIb,而2023年在刚果出现了Clade Ib,随后持续传播并扩散至非洲以外地区。与Clade IIb相比,Clade Ib被认为与更严重的临床结局和持续的人际传播有关,对儿童、孕妇及免疫功能低下人群构成更大威胁。 然而,传统非人灵长类动物模型成本高、实验周期长,CAST/EiJ等易感小鼠又存在繁殖困难、供应受限等问题。因此,建立来源稳定、操作方便且能够反映不同疾病严重程度的小鼠模型,特别是建立评价疫苗小鼠模型,是开展猴痘病毒研究的迫切需求。 内接种方式,以相同剂量的MPXV Clade Ib感染四种不同遗传背景的小鼠(C57BL/6小鼠、 BALB/c小鼠、Stat1基因敲除小鼠和AGB6小鼠),结果显示,四种小鼠感染后均出现不同程度的体重下降,但疾病结局存在明显差异。 其中,STAT1缺失小鼠表现出最高易感性,在感染后第8天前后达到100%死亡;AGB6小鼠死亡率约为40%。相比之下,C57BL/6和BALB/c小鼠虽然出现一过性体重下降,但均能够存活并逐渐恢复,表现为自限性感染。 病毒学和病理学检测进一步发现,病毒能够在小鼠鼻甲和肺组织中有效复制。肺组织中的病毒抗原主要分布于支气管上皮及其周围炎症细胞,STAT1缺失小鼠的病毒抗原信号和肺部损伤最为明显。这些结果提示,宿主干扰素信号通路是限制Clade Ib复制和疾病进展的重要防线。 (Stat1敲除小鼠、AGB6 小鼠与野生型小鼠对猴痘病毒 Ib 分支的易感性差异) 不同遗传背景决定不同免疫响应节奏 为了进一步解析宿主免疫反应,研究团队对感染后不同时间点的C57BL/6和BALB/c小鼠脾脏进行了转录组测序。 结果显示,C57BL/6小鼠能够较早启动强烈的抗病毒反应。感染后第3天,便可检测到大量差异表达基因,Oas1a、Rtp1和Ligp1等抗病毒相关基因明显上调;感染后第5天,差异表达基因数量达到峰值。相比之下,BALB/c小鼠的转录反应出现得更晚,整体幅度也相对较弱。 值得注意的是,尽管两种小鼠均激活了干扰素和炎症相关通路,但其适应性免疫相关基因却出现不同程度下调。 C57BL/6小鼠主要表现为淋巴细胞分化和功能相关通路受抑,而BALB/c小鼠则更多表现为MHC抗原加工与呈递通路下调。 进入恢复期后,C57BL/6小鼠逐渐启动细胞增殖、细胞外基质重塑和组织修复相关程序;BALB/c小鼠则在较晚阶段出现免疫球蛋白介导的免疫反应。 这说明,Clade Ib感染不仅能诱导强烈的先天免疫和炎症反应,还可能伴随适应性免疫相关程序的暂时抑制,而这种免疫失衡具有明显的宿主遗传背景差异。 (C57BL/6与Balb/c小鼠感染猴痘病毒Ib分支后脾脏转录组的时间动态变化) Clade Ib表现出更快的感染进程 研究团队进一步在易感的Stat1缺失小鼠中,以相同感染剂量和相同实验条件比较了Clade Ib与Clade IIb的毒力。 结果显示,与Clade IIb相比,Clade Ib感染后小鼠体重下降出现得更早,疾病进展更快,肺组织病毒载量更高,病毒抗原分布也更加广泛。 转录组分析发现,Clade Ib感染伴随更明显的组织损伤和炎症相关表达特征,包括Mmp8和S100a3等基因上调。同时,干扰素应答、抗原加工与呈递等免疫相关通路呈现更广泛的下调。 不过,在所检测时间点的肺组织病理评分并未出现显著差异。综上所述,现有结果支持Clade Ib在该模型中具有更快的感染动力学和更强的复制能力。 (Stat1 基因敲除小鼠中猴痘病毒Ib 分支与 IIb 分支的致病性比较) 特考玮瑞显著抑制病毒复制 为了验证这些小鼠模型是否可用于抗病毒药物评价,研究团队选择正痘病毒抑制剂特考玮瑞进行体内实验。 在C57BL/6、AGB6和Stat1缺失小鼠中,特考玮瑞均能够减轻感染后的体重下降,并明显降低肺组织中的病毒载量和病毒抗原水平。 组织病理学结果也显示,药物处理后小鼠肺组织结构保存更完整,炎症、坏死及其他感染相关损伤得到改善。 转录组结果表明,特考玮瑞治疗还可减弱病毒感染引起的大规模转录重塑,使宿主转录状态向创伤修复和恢复相关程序转变。 需要注意的是,本研究中的特考玮瑞在感染当天即开始给药,属于非常早期的干预模式。 (验证AGB6、Stat1缺失以及C57BL/6 小鼠作为猴痘病毒 Ib 分支药物评价模型的适用性) 研究意义 本研究建立了野生型、干扰素受体缺失和STAT1缺失小鼠Clade Ib感染的模型体系。 不同模型可满足不同研究需求: 野生型小鼠适合用于研究非致死性病毒复制、宿主免疫反应,以及药物和疫苗评价; AGB6小鼠可用于研究中度至重度感染; Stat1缺失小鼠则能够形成快速进展的致死性疾病,适合开展致病性和抗病毒药物的初步体内评价。 研究还从转录组层面揭示了Clade Ib感染过程中“先天免疫和炎症激活-适应性免疫相关程序下调-组织修复启动”的动态变化,为理解宿主遗传背景、干扰素信号和疾病严重程度之间的关系提供了实验数据。 作者信息 广州医科大学附属市八医院与山西农业大学联合培养博士生韩红宇、硕士生王肖玮为该论文共同第一作者,广州医科大学附属市八医院唐小平教授、于海生教授和山西农业大学庞全海教授为本文的共同通讯作者。 于海生教授,广州医科大学附属市八医院PI,传染病研究所副所长(主持工作),生物安全三级实验室副主任。长期从事新突发病毒的感染与免疫相关研究,致力于树突状细胞在病毒感染中作用、中和抗体研发以及研究高致病性病毒的致病机理。以第一作者或通讯作者在Molecular Therapy(2026)、National Science Review(2025)、Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy(2023)、Nature Communications(2023)、JCI Insight(2020)等杂志发表 SCI 文章50余篇。主持或参与国家传染病重大专项、省自然科学基金、科技攻关专项等项目。 Free web novels for online reading. 评论 全部 还没有人评论过,快来抢首评 抢首评 推荐阅读 analysis.time: The study was published on 2026-08-16. The research findings were based on data from 2022 and 2023, with the experimental results from the study conducted in 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The research was conducted using mouse models, including C57BL/6, BALB/c, Stat1 gene knockout, and AGB6 mice, which are laboratory animals. The study focused on the monkeypox virus (MPXV) Clade Ib and its impact on these models.
analysis.event: A research team from Guangzhou Eighth People's Hospital and Shanxi Agricultural University published a study on the pathogenic characteristics of MPXV Clade Ib in laboratory mouse models. The study compared the disease outcomes and immune responses of different mouse strains infected with Clade Ib and Clade IIb, and evaluated the antiviral drug tecovirimat.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study found that Clade Ib caused more severe disease outcomes in mice compared to Clade IIb, with Stat1 gene knockout mice showing 100% mortality by day 8. The research also highlighted the potential of tecovirimat to reduce viral replication and disease severity in these models. The findings suggest that Clade Ib poses a greater threat to immunocompromised individuals and may have more severe clinical outcomes.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was conducted in a laboratory setting using mouse models. The research team established a system of mouse models to evaluate the pathogenicity and antiviral effects of MPXV Clade Ib. The results are based on experimental data and are not related to real-world outbreaks or public health responses.

analysis.brief_en: A research team from Guangzhou Eighth People's Hospital and Shanxi Agricultural University published a study on the pathogenic characteristics of MPXV Clade Ib in laboratory mouse models. The study compared the disease outcomes and immune responses of different mouse strains infected with Clade Ib and Clade IIb, and evaluated the antiviral drug tecovirimat. news.content_title: Will the next pandemic be spotted in a hospital or under London’s streets?
news.content: Will the next pandemic be spotted in a hospital or under London’s streets? You probably don’t need reminding that Covid brought the country and the capital to its knees. It snuck up on us thanks to the speed of modern-day air travel — putting London right in the crosshairs of the pandemic. Since then, time, effort, and political and scientific capital has been invested to try and give us a headstart on identifying, then heading off, the next pandemic before it begins. And much of this work focuses on what we flush down our toilets and what passes under Londoners’ feet every day through its sewers. The UK has built an end-to-end wastewater system across 31 sites, testing for 12 priority pathogens that could cause problems to public health. Over the next year, ministers want to expand environmental surveillance across sewers, hospitals and transport settings. A separate pandemic preparedness plan says the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) will explore sampling aircraft wastewater to detect diseases arriving in Britain. “Wastewater tells no lies — everything we do in society is reflected in the wastewater” Davey Jones, professor of environmental science and public health at Bangor University The Government’s UK Biological Security Strategy, published in July, sets out plans to connect different forms of disease surveillance, while UKHSA is spending £1.3 million testing whether wastewater can reveal genetic traces of pathogens including Mpox and West Nile virus. “Wastewater tells no lies,” says Davey Jones, professor of environmental science and public health at Bangor University. “Everything we do in society is reflected in the wastewater.” We already check wastewater for the presence of polio. Earlier this year, the tracking of wastewater found two indications of vaccine-derived poliovirus in sewage samples taken from London. That was important because Australia — with whom London has regular flight connections — had a small spate of similar results. But indications in such small numbers in London are routine, and didn’t require any public health intervention, authorities said. Constructing a viral family tree It was a very different situation in 2022, when genetically linked detections occurring time and time again suggested there was person-to-person transmission in north and east London. That outbreak prompted a vaccination campaign within areas of the capital. Polio is a special case because Britain has monitored sewage for it routinely since 2014. But it also shows that it’s possible for scientists to separate nascent outbreaks from the biological background noise. “You have the pathogen in the sample, so you can sequence it,” says Nicholas Grassly, professor of infectious disease and vaccine epidemiology at Imperial College London. With more than one detection, researchers can construct a viral family tree, he explains, helping them understand “where it’s come from”. But it’s harder than it first seems. “Picking up a signal is extremely difficult if you don’t know what you’re looking for,” says Barbara Kasprzyk-Hordern, who leads the University of Bath’s Centre of Excellence in Water-Based Early-Warning Systems for Health Protection. That means that wastewater analysis is just one weapon in the arsenal that needs to be used to tackle potential problems before they arise. While wastewater can indicate where officials should look, doctors and laboratories need to establish whether people are becoming ill and what treatment is needed. Grassly describes wastewater as “a free biological sample from hundreds of thousands of individuals”, one that can indicate how widespread an infection is without requiring each person to come forward for testing. The same sample can also be searched for several pathogens at once. That means health authorities can track common illnesses such as Covid, flu, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), measles and polio while looking for rarer virus signatures in the background. A signal from the airplane loo Aircraft toilets could add another layer. In a 2022 UK study, researchers sampled sewage from terminals and 32 aircraft at Heathrow, Bristol and Edinburgh airports. At the peak of the pandemic, 93 per cent of aircraft samples contained SARS-CoV-2 — the virus that caused Covid. The Government now wants to evaluate whether similar methods could flag imported diseases without swabbing passengers individually — helping scale up detection of potential problems before they arise. The ability of wastewater to survey whole populations without identifying individuals is a massive advantage and can help identify from where outbreaks occurred, and help snub them out before they become significant. “We never know who is ill,” says Kasprzyk-Hordern. “But we know how communities were exposed.” Once signs that something is wrong appears in wastewater, conventional testing can be used to find out whether people are infected and whether an intervention is required. Grassly points out that there is another limitation. Finding a virus at Heathrow may buy Britain several days or perhaps a week compared with hospital detection — but it also means the pathogen is already travelling internationally. His Wastewater Surveillance for Pandemic Prevention network is therefore looking further upstream, in communities in Africa and South-east Asia where animal viruses repeatedly spill into people. Those small spillovers are “the sparks of the fire”, Grassly says. Detecting them early could allow safer market practices or interventions in livestock before an outbreak becomes a global emergency. “The biggest benefit will be when we align all the pieces of information together,” says Kasprzyk-Hordern, including what is happening at the clinical, community and environmental levels. “We’re not there yet.” But with work, it’s possible to be. As Grassly puts it, “prevention is going to be much easier than being responsive”. analysis.brief_en: The United Kingdom is scaling up environmental surveillance to detect priority pathogens, including mpox, as part of pandemic preparedness. UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) is investing £1.3 million to test wastewater for genetic traces of mpox and West Nile virus, while ministers plan to expand monitoring across sewers, hospitals, and transport hubs, including aircraft toilets. This initiative follows earlier wastewater detections of vaccine-derived poliovirus in London, which did not require public health intervention. Experts note wastewater can provide early signals of community-level infection without individual testing, but emphasize it must be combined with clinical and laboratory confirmation. The approach aims to identify emerging threats before they escalate, though challenges remain in distinguishing meaningful signals from background noise.
